channel: A — inverted funnel (new both-real optimization rows)
recruitment_law: selection is blind to locality; admission is on charge-citability ONLY.
admission_criterion: the problem is an OPTIMIZATION problem (has a well-defined objective to min/max),
AND it is NOT already an atlas_v3 problem_id (genuinely new),

AND BOTH gradient charges are plausibly citable at R20: a known approximation status (scheme / const / log / poly / inapprox) AND a known parameterized status (FPT / W[t] / para-NP-hard / XP) from the standard literature.
sealed_sources: the parameterized-approximation surveys' problem lists (Feldmann–Karthik–Lee–Manurangsi and successors),
kernelization compendia / the parameterized-algorithms textbook problem index (Cygan et al.) — both-real by construction (kernel papers state param status and usually approx context),
the W-hierarchy classified problem lists × the approximation compendium (Ausiello–Kann) intersection.
selection_order: candidates enumerated in the fixed source order above, then alphabetically by problem name WITHIN each source; the FIRST N meeting the admission criterion are drafted. Order is fixed before any locality read; no reordering by anticipated structure/stratum.
explicitly_forbidden: selecting or reordering a candidate because of its anticipated locality class, its structure, or which stratum is thin. The recruitment artifacts never mention locality.
instrument: new rows drafted at 'claimed', dual-pass Check-9, owner confirm sittings, S2 dedup, provenance — standard pipeline. Locality coding (blind 3-class qualified instrument) runs at Q3 AFTER charges, never during selection.
